description: Argo is a student team from the University of Belgrade designing space systems
summary:
Margo is an interactive web application that hosts localized Mars areas, and enables users to navigate desired regions. We chose four specific regions: Gale crater, Jezero crater, Opportunity landing site and Mawrth Vallis. Some were chosen as a well known spots where we have gathered a lot of data, others for their geological composition.

We made an interactive map that helps astronauts plan and perform complex Mars missions.
Margo is a fully featured experience packed with information that aims to help human explorers achieve advancements in space research.
details:
Margo is an interactive Mars exploration platform that helps astronauts plan surface missions. It combines layered maps, 3D terrain, geological composition, and route planning to make Mars data useful for navigation, safety, and scientific research.

SCOPE AND WORKINGS OF THE APPLICATION

Users begin on an interactive 3D globe and select one of four regions: Gale Crater, Jezero Crater, the Opportunity landing site, or Mawrth Vallis. The application then opens a dedicated sector map with base imagery, elevation, thermal, and radiation-related layers.

Astronauts can inspect the landscape in 2D or 3D, display multiple layers, and locate recorded mineral detections that could become research destinations.

Users place waypoints and choose a walker or rover profile. The pathfinding algorithm calculates a route that balances distance, terrain hazards, and steep slopes. Results include estimated travel time, distance, ascent, descent, an elevation profile, and modelled radiation exposure. Blocked or incomplete routes are clearly identified.

A planned extension will let base-station crews download selected sectors before missions for offline use.

PURPOSE

Margo brings navigation, environmental context, and scientific targets into one interface. It helps crews assess difficult terrain, understand the demands of a journey, and plan visits to areas of scientific interest.

Travel estimates account for slope and roughness, while separate walker and rover profiles represent different mobility assumptions. The 3D view makes terrain easier to understand, and mineral markers help connect route planning with research objectives.

IMPACT

Our immediate goal is to demonstrate how Mars datasets can support practical surface mission planning.

Our long-term vision is to support crew autonomy: helping astronauts use locally available information to assess routes and pursue scientific objectives despite communication delays with Earth.

TECHNOLOGIES

• Frontend: Angular, TypeScript, HTML, and CSS.

• Mapping: OpenLayers for 2D maps and Three.js for the globe and 3D terrain. gdal and qgis for map files processing.

• Pathfinding: Custom A* implementations with weighted terrain hazards and slope penalties.

• Scientific references: Mars raster datasets, CRISM and OMEGA mineral records, radiation level and NASA’s Mars24 approach for local time.

• Development: Angular CLI, npm, Node.js, Vitest, and Docker.

THE CREATIVITY

Margo connects planetary exploration with the practical decisions involved in a Marswalk. Users move from a global view to a selected sector, inspect its environment, choose scientific destinations, and evaluate a route.

Its interactive 3D layer stack helps users compare different datasets over the same landscape. Combining mineral locations with terrain-aware routing connects scientific opportunity with mission demands.

The result translates complex information into concrete questions: Where should we go? How difficult is the journey? How long could it take? What could we study there?

CONSIDERATIONS

Safety: Hazard-sensitive routing, steep-transition restrictions, exposure estimates, and clear warnings for unreachable destinations.

Mobility: Separate walker and rover profiles reflect differences in speed, terrain sensitivity, and shielding assumptions.

Data limitations: Routing depends on map resolution; identifying individual rocks and small holes requires finer data. Travel and radiation figures are prototype estimates requiring further validation.

FUTURE

Future operations: Downloadable sectors are planned to support missions with limited connectivity. HUD integration for accessibility. Integrating the webapp into an app format.
